title: Operator field notes — lossy streams & rate-error patterns
summary: Concise on-call reference for recurring API failure modes where streaming degrades, timeouts rise, or 429s spike. Focused on fast triage, short mitigations, and evidence to collect for post-incident debugging.
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact operator reference for the most common degradation triage paths we see: timeouts, elevated 429s (rate-limit responses), and partially degraded streaming (clients see truncated streams, long initial latency, or keepalive drops). Aim: get customer-facing traffic back to baseline within 15–30 minutes, gather debug artifacts, and hand to eng for root cause follow-up.

Scope / When to use:
- Pager or alert: streaming error rate > 0.5% or 5xxs > 2% sustained for 5m, or 429 spike above baseline (5x)
- Symptoms: incomplete stream chunks, repeated client reconnects, long TTFB for streaming sessions, growth in request timeouts, sudden jump in 429 headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining approaches 0)

Quick triage (0–5m):
1) Confirm alert context: check alert page (Alert: API High Error Rate) for threshold, scope, and impacted routes.
2) Identify blast radius: query Grafana dashboard "api-traffic-overview" with group by route/model/region.
   - Command: (example) curl -s https://grafana/api/datasource/proxy/1/query -d 'query=...'
3) Look for correlation: fallback model usage, capacity events, or infra deploys in last 15m (check #deploys channel or /deployments dashboard).
4) Immediate mitigation options (pick one, apply, observe 1–3 minutes):
   - If 429 spike: temporarily raise per-tenant rate limit (if safe) or enable tiered-fallback to a cheaper model variant to reduce load.
   - If timeouts across many routes: increase proxy timeout (ingress/nginx/proxy) by small step (e.g., +2s) while analyzing.
   - If streaming truncation: reduce max chunk size or enable chunked-keepalive (see feature flag stream-keepalive-on).
5) Notify stakeholders in incident thread (#sre-incidents) with initial findings and mitigation applied.

Data to collect (1–10m):
- Sample request/response traces from tracing service (trace ids), rough timestamps, and affected routes.
- Host-level metrics for GPUs/CPUs: top-10 high CPU/GPU hosts in last 10m.
- Proxy/LB logs: 502/504 patterns, connection resets, upstream disconnects.
- Model-serving logs: sequence length distribution & KV cache hit ratio (if available).
- Any recent autoscaler events (scale-up/scale-down cycles).
- Client-side error patterns: are clients retrying aggressively? check client user-agent heatmap.

Deeper diagnostics (10–30m):
A) Timeouts dominant:
  - Check ingress timeouts vs runtime timeouts. Common misalignment: ingress timeout < runtime max processing time -> 504s seen at edge while runtime keeps processing.
  - Commands: kubectl logs -n runtime pod/xxx | grep 'request-id' ; check envoy stats: envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_timeouts.
  - If runtime CPU/GPU hot: check batch queue length and continuous batching config. Short-term: reduce batch window to favor latency.
  - Long-term: capacity plan for peak sequence length distribution.

B) 429s spike:
  - Confirm whether 429s are emitted by edge quota layer or by model serving. Inspect X-RateLimit-* headers and the issuer service in access logs.
  - If edge quota: it's usually intended; check sudden traffic from single API key/tenant. If so, throttle that key or contact customer.
  - If service-side 429 (backpressure): check autoscaler saturation and circuit-breaker triggers. Short-term: enable fallback route to a compatible model variant with looser QPS.
  - If client retries cause storming: add short jittered retry advice to SDK docs and adjust server Retry-After header.

C) Degraded streaming (partial frames, long initial TTFB):
  - Inspect keepalive stats between ingress <-> runtime. If connection drops at ~60s consistently, likely a proxy idle timeout.
  - Check chunk sizes and buffer flushing. Some runtime optimizations can delay first chunk to coalesce tokens; set stream-early-flush flag for affected routes.
  - If memory pressure or GC spikes observed, check model quantization variant and memory footprint.

Short-term mitigation templates (safe ops):
- "Enable streaming keepalive": flip feature flag stream-keepalive-on for specific route (console or feature-flag CLI).
- "Temporary rate cap per-key": create short-lived policy 30m window for offending key (use admin console).
- "Fallback to smaller model": update routing policy for affected route to fallback-target: model-small-v2 for 60m.
- "Increase proxy timeout": patch ingress config map: timeout: 20s -> 22s; rollout to edge proxies.

Rollback criteria / Safety checks:
- Any config change must have rollback play documented in the incident thread.
- If raising timeouts or changing routing, monitor error spikes and token-cost impact.
- If mitigation increases token spend >20% over baseline, escalate to cost-owner.

Post-incident evidence to collect for RCA:
- Representative trace ids and full spans.
- Timeline of mitigation steps with timestamps and person who executed.
- Metric deltas (p50/p95 latency, error rate, 429s count, stream success rate) before/after.
- Autoscaler events and logs, recent deploy IDs and PR links.
- Any correlated infra events (cloud provider spot preemptions, network flaps).

Common root causes we've seen (notes):
- Sudden client-side retry storms after brief outage -> 429s then cascading 5xx. Prevention: SDK default backoff + jitter.
- Misaligned timeout defaults (ingress 15s vs runtime 25s) -> client sees 504, retries, and box-jams.
- Batch-window misconfiguration: optimized for cost, inadvertently increases p95 latency on long-seq workloads.
- Feature-flaged kernel path causing larger-than-expected GC pauses on certain models.

Communication template (incident status update):
- Short: "Oncall investigating increased 429s for /v1/chat; applied temporary rate cap to offending key and enabled fallback to model-small-v2. Observing error rate decrease from 4.3% -> 0.9%. Collecting traces; ETA for update 20m."

Checklist before handoff to Eng RCA team:
- Collected logs/metrics and stored snapshot in S3 (link).
- Tagged incident with suspected root cause class (timeouts|backpressure|client-retries|proxy-timeout).
- Created follow-up ticket with priority and acceptance criteria for fix.
- Added recommended long-term mitigations (SDK backoff defaults, aligned timeouts, capacity buffer).

Short operator tips / heuristics (quick brain shortcuts):
- If only one region is affected, think infra (AZ/host) or regional autoscaler issues.
- If all routes to a specific model show problems, suspect the model-serving pool (quantization patch, kernel update).
- 429s + high queue length on runtime = internal backpressure; 429s alone with normal queue length = edge policy enforcement.
- Watch for correlated increases in model token-generation time when sequence length distribution changes.

Open TODOs and follow-ups:
- Add a small runbook snippet to SDK repo for recommended retry behavior (owner: devx).
- Instrument a short-lived "early-flush" metric to make streaming first-chunk latency visible (owner: serving-runtime).
- Bake a default ingress/runtime timeout alignment test into deployment pipeline (owner: platform-engineering).

Notes to self / operator reminders:
- Keep mitigation steps minimal and reversible.
- When in doubt, prefer routing to a compatible smaller model over large global timeout changes.
- Always capture trace ids before doing mass rollbacks (trace ids are the single most useful artifact).

Appendix: Useful dashboards and queries
- Grafana: api-traffic-overview, streaming-latency-first-chunk, model-pool-health
- Loki queries: {app="ingress"} | json | status=~"5.."
- Tracing: search by operation.name="/v1/chat" and span.tag(request_id)
